# **Data Exploration**
***

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
sample_metadata <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "imported", "sample_metadata.csv"))
```

Now that you've imported the data, let's take a look at it. We'll use the function `glimpse()`, from the `dplyr` package that we've already been working with. This function shows the first several observations from each column of our dataset.

::: {.rcode}
```{r}
glimpse(sample_metadata)
```
:::

:::{.think_question}
::::{.think_question_header}
Question opportunity
::::
::::{.inner_block}
As we described in the ["What are the data?" section](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-version-control/#what-are-the-data), the variables that we will use in our analysis are `Study`, `SampleID`, `PersonID`, `Category`, `Sampling from papers`, and `Sampling, day`. What appears to be the difference between `Sampling from papers` and `Sampling, day`? 

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The variable `Sampling, day` is encoded with numeric values (this represents the day since birth on which the sample was taken), while the variable `Sampling from paper` is a character vector. For the first several observations shown in `glimpse()`, this describes the month at which the sample was taken. This varies across studies; in other studies `Sampling from paper` describes the day of sampling. `Sampling, day` is a variable added by @wang2021metagenomic in their {{< glossary "meta-analysis" >}} to compare sampling timing across studies on the same scale.

</details>
::::
:::
